newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel defence ministry to request extra funds.
newsitem.headline: Israel defence ministry to request extra funds.

text.p: Israel's Defence Ministry intends to request a supplementary budget to cover costs incurred by the army during recent clashes with Palestinians, ministry sources said on Monday.
"We haven't yet made any decisions regarding the final costs of the clashes," a source said. "But we intend to ask for a supplementary budget."
The source said the budget requested would be for 1996, but could not say when the request would be put to the Treasury.
The Treasury has said there would be no increase in the budget to finance the costs of the clashes.
Gunbattles between Israeli soldiers and Palestinians that claimed 74 lives erupted when Israel opened an additional entry to a tunnel in Jerusalem, near Islam's third holiest site.
Israel and the Palestinians started talks on Sunday to end the tensions and continue the peace process.
Israel's daily Yedioth Ahronoth reported that the Treasury estimated the costs of the clashes at 200 million to 300 million shekels.
The 1996 defence budget totalled 27.41 billion shekels, including $1.8 billion in U.S. aid.

The government has approved a cut of 4.9 billion shekels in the overall budget in 1997 including 825 million from the 30 billion shekels allocated for defence. Parliament has until the end of the year to vote on the budget.
